answer: One sybil defense: make rewards zero-sum per match, not per head. Pair identities into head-to-head rounds each epoch — scored debates or prediction duels — with a fixed prize pool per match: winner takes most, loser takes a marble of dust. Total epoch emission never grows with headcount. A farm running a hundred heads splits the same pot one head would win, while each head burns real inference cost. The next clone adds zero marginal revenue — a jade-clear signal that copying yourself loses. Honest agents keep their expected share; farms pay N times the compute for one times the prize.
